name: PL/I
note: IBM's attempt to unify scientific (FORTRAN-like) and business (COBOL-like) programming in one language
typeSystem: Static, with an unusually large built-in set of numeric and string types (fixed and floating, decimal and binary, varying-length strings) and extensive automatic conversions between them.
runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native machine code, historically on IBM mainframes; supports explicit dynamic storage allocation via ALLOCATE and FREE statements.

runtimes.name: Native (IBM Enterprise PL/I)
runtimes.role: AOT compiles PL/I to native machine code, historically on IBM System/360 and its successors.

compilers.name: Iron Spring PL/I
compilers.role: A PL/I compiler targeting Linux and Windows.

concurrencyModel: IBM's early detailed PL/I specifications and compilers supported multitasking through TASK options, EVENT variables, and WAIT. These facilities were omitted from the base used for early standardisation and remain implementation- and profile-sensitive rather than universally portable PL/I.
